summary: Exiting world does not release file handle to zipped datapack / resourcepack
description:
open Minecraft

open a world that contains a zipped datapack in its datapacks directory

after world is loaded, save & exit back to title screen

in windows file explorer, navigate to datapacks directory and try to delete the .zip file of the datapack

EXPECTED:

file can be deleted

ACTUAL:

file cannot be deleted because it is still in use by java process (Minecraft sitting at title screen)

NOTES:

you can work around it by closing Minecraft, or by opening a different world (at which point MC seems to 'flush' its datapacks)

Ideally, Minecraft should only be using the file during load/reload - once loading is complete, it should release the file handle. (for non-zip files, like functions in a datapack, you can delete each while the world is loaded)

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft version 20w17a.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. From the Singleplayer world list, select the world, choose Edit, and select Open World Folder.
4. Open the world’s `datapacks` directory in Windows File Explorer and place a zipped datapack named `my-datapack.zip` in it.
5. Return to Minecraft and load the world.
6. Select Esc menu -> Save and Quit to Title.
7. In Windows File Explorer, navigate to the world’s `datapacks` directory and try to delete `my-datapack.zip`.
8. Observe that the file cannot be deleted because it is still in use by the Minecraft Java process while Minecraft is at the title screen.
Observed Behavior:
After saving and exiting the world to the title screen, Minecraft continues to hold an open file handle to the world’s zipped datapack (`<world>/datapacks/my-datapack.zip`). On Windows, attempting to delete the ZIP file in File Explorer fails because it is still in use by the Minecraft Java process.

The file remains locked while Minecraft is at the title screen and can only be deleted after closing Minecraft or opening another world, which appears to release the datapack resources. The failure produces a `java.nio.file.FileSystemException` indicating that the process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
Expected Behavior: After saving and exiting a world, Minecraft should release any file handles associated with its zipped datapacks, allowing the `.zip` file to be deleted or modified from Windows File Explorer while the game remains at the title screen. The file should not remain locked by the Minecraft Java process after world loading or reloading is complete.
